common_name: Control Oilseed Radish (Nematode-Suppressive Biofumigant Cover Crop Radish)

planting.note: Broadcast or drill into a firm, well-prepared seedbed 6 to 10 weeks before the first fall frost so plants build a full rosette and root system before killing cold arrives.

directions: Control is an oilseed radish cultivar bred for pest suppression rather than deep tillage, relying on a spreading lateral and fibrous root system instead of one long daikon-type taproot to loosen surface soil and scavenge residual nitrogen. Its primary value is as a biofumigant: glucosinolate compounds released as roots and residue break down help suppress plant-parasitic nematodes and some soilborne pathogens ahead of a following cash crop. Dense, fast top growth shades out fall weed flushes, and compared with daikon-type tillage radishes its decomposing residue produces noticeably less of the sulfurous odor common to the group. A hard freeze reliably winterkills the crop in most temperate regions, after which growers can no-till plant directly into the collapsed residue the following spring without additional termination steps.
